skills.name: create-skill
skills.description: Interactive skill generator that scaffolds new skills following all project conventions, serving as the definitive reference for skill creation.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user wants to create a new Claude Code skill, asks how to package a workflow as a skill, or describes a repeatable procedure they want callable as `/something`.

skills.name: dep-check
skills.description: Scans all dependency declarations across ecosystems, checks for updates and vulnerabilities, and produces a prioritized update plan with testing recommendations.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user asks about outdated dependencies, package CVEs, pinned-version freshness, dependabot/renovate gaps, or wants an upgrade plan across ecosystems (npm, pip, cargo, go, gem, composer, docker, GitHub Actions).

skills.name: diagnose
skills.description: Multi-agent root cause analysis that traces errors, correlates with recent changes, and identifies fixes with ranked hypotheses.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user pastes an error message or stack trace, reports unexpected behavior, asks "why is X failing", or wants help finding the root cause of a CI/test failure.

skills.name: docstring-check
skills.description: Scans a codebase for missing, outdated, drifted, or inconsistent docstrings and applies behavior-preserving fixes matching the project's detected convention.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user asks about missing/outdated docstrings, signature-vs-doc drift, docstring coverage on the public API, or wants to align documentation to a detected project style (Google/NumPy/reST/TSDoc/JSDoc/godoc/rustdoc/Javadoc).

skills.name: enhance
skills.description: Performs deep multi-phase project analysis to identify and recommend the single most impactful addition to implement.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user wants a strategic deep-dive that recommends the single highest-impact addition to build next — not a code review or a list of improvements. User-triggered only.

skills.name: github-audit
skills.description: Audits a GitHub repository against best practices and provides prioritized recommendations for README, license, community health, CI/CD, and repository settings.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user asks for a GitHub repo audit, wants to evaluate README/license/community-health/CI-CD coverage, or asks "is this repo ready for public release".

skills.name: github-ship
skills.description: Turns local changes into a GitHub issue and linked PR, or cleans up the branch if the PR was already merged. Auto-detects which.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user wants to ship pending changes as a GitHub issue + PR pair, or wants to clean up a feature branch after the PR has been merged on GitHub. Auto-detects create vs cleanup mode.

skills.name: idiom-check
skills.description: Audits a codebase through a programming-language-specific idiom lens, produces a prioritized report, and offers remediation in PR-sized bundles.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user asks for a language-specific idiom audit (e.g., "are we writing idiomatic Rust", "is this Pythonic", "Go-style review") of the whole codebase. Distinct from /vet (which works on a diff) and /refactor (single target).

skills.name: refactor
skills.description: Comprehensive code refactoring across correctness, security, performance, and maintainability with behavior-preserving, incremental changes.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user wants to refactor a specific file/module/function — distinct from /vet (which works on a diff) and /idiom-check (which audits the whole codebase through one language lens).

skills.name: test-gen
skills.description: Analyzes code to generate comprehensive tests covering happy paths, edge cases, error handling, and integration points, matching the project's existing test conventions.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user asks to generate, write, or create tests for a specific file, function, class, or directory. Also after a refactor or bug fix when the user wants regression coverage.

skills.name: vet
skills.description: Structured code review across correctness, security, performance, and conventions with prioritized findings and fix offers.
skills.when_to_use: Use when the user asks for a review of pending changes, wants a verdict on a diff, asks "is this ready to merge", or names a file/branch/commit-range to review.
